'''''Cistus'' × ''purpureus''''', commonly known as '''orchid rockrose''', is one of the most commonly cultivated varieties of [[Cistus|rockrose]].<ref name=Sheat/> 

==Description==
It is a small and bushy subshrub that grows 120cm to 180cm high and wide with wavy, dense, dull green leaves.<ref>[https://www.gardenia.net/plant/cistus-purpureus-purple-flowered-rock-rose Cistus purpureus] by gardenia.net</ref>

The pink flowers, which appear from spring to summer, are 8cm (3 in) across that have petals with a dark blotch towards the centre. Each flower lasts a day, though a succession of flowers appear throughout the flowering season.<ref name=Sheat>{{cite book|author1=Sheat, W.G. |author2=Gerald Schofield |title=Complete Gardening in Southern Africa|publisher=Struik Publishers|year=1995|page=47|isbn=978-1-86825-704-1}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The hybrid [[cultivar]] was first formally described in 1786 by [[Jean-Baptiste Lamarck]] in the [[botany]] division of the ''[[Encyclopédie Méthodique|Encyclopédie méthodique par ordre des matières]]''.<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate=27 May 2011}}</ref>
